objectives.statement: Identify LINQ standard query operators as extension members that provide filtering, projection, sorting, grouping and other operations over sequences.
Explain deferred execution as constructing a query whose operator logic runs when the resulting sequence is enumerated.
Distinguish Select as a projection that produces one result per source element from SelectMany, which flattens subsequences.
Identify Where as the standard query operator that selects sequence values according to a predicate function.
objectives.citation: Filtering Data in C# with LINQ

objectives.statement: Relate common query-expression clauses such as where, select, orderby and join to their standard query operators.
Compare LINQ over IEnumerable<T>, whose operator logic runs during enumeration, with LINQ over IQueryable<T>, whose query is represented as an expression tree for provider translation.
Explain that OrderBy and orderby arrange query results according to a key selector, with descending variants available.
Identify GroupBy as the operator that groups elements sharing a common attribute and represents each group as an IGrouping<TKey,TElement>.
Explain that Join performs an equijoin by matching key selectors and that the ordinary Join returns only matching elements.
Distinguish GroupJoin as correlating sequences while grouping the matching elements for each element of the first sequence.
Identify Distinct and DistinctBy as set operators that remove duplicate values, with DistinctBy using a key selector as the discriminator.
Explain that Any returns a Boolean indicating whether any sequence element satisfies a condition, or whether a sequence contains an element.
Distinguish the quantifier operators All, Any and Contains by the Boolean question each asks about a sequence.
Explain Skip and Take as partitioning operators that respectively omit an initial number of elements and retain an initial number of elements.
Compare Select and SelectMany when a transform returns a sequence: Select preserves one result per source element, while SelectMany concatenates the subsequences.
Identify LeftJoin and RightJoin in .NET 10 as outer equijoins that retain unmatched elements from the left or right sequence respectively.
Diagnose a query over IQueryable<T> as provider-translatable through an expression tree, whereas a query over IEnumerable<T> executes operator logic during enumeration.
Explain why constructing a deferred LINQ query does not by itself enumerate the source or produce its final results.
Apply GroupBy with a subsequent projection over each IGrouping to produce a result based on group keys and group contents.
Diagnose an exception or changed source observation that appears only while iterating a LINQ result as a consequence of deferred query execution.
